full_judgment: 2. Defendant is the petitioner. The plaintiffs brought the suit for specific performance of contract for sale. The suit was ex-parte decreed on 19.12.81. Thereafter Order 9 Rule 13 proceeding was initiated by the defendants, being Miscellaneous Case No. 167 of 1982. The same case is still pending. The petitioners prayed for opinion of the hand-writing expert to ascertain whether the alleged, signature and initials of the petitioners are genuine or forged. This petition was rejected. Thereafter the High Court Division was moved and a Division Bench took the view that no illegality was committed by the trial court which requires interference. It was noted in the High Court Division that the Court is at liberty to compare the signatures of the petitioners and the view was expressed that it is for the Court to decide whether it will compare the signature in exercise of powers under Section 73 of the Evidence Act or it will send to the hand-writing expert. Since the trial court rejected the prayer for opinion of the hand-writing expert, no illegality was com-mitted. In this view of the matter the application was summarily rejected.
